title: What are the numbers of floors B, C, F, G and H?
description: Three floors of the line carry numbers, and the other floors are found by counting ticks up or down from a known floor. One floor is checked by counting from a second known floor.
teaching_notes: One idea: count ticks from a floor whose number is known. Watch for students who write the number of ticks as the number of the floor.

video_script.why: The child finds the number of a floor by counting ticks from a floor whose number is known.
video_script.substitution: the book's own line of lettered floors, with floors A, D and E given
video_script.anchor: the lettered floors of Ruhee drawn as a line with ticks
video_script.payoff_line: Count the ticks from a floor you know to find the number of any floor.

final_answer.spoken: floor B is minus nine, floor C is minus six, floor F is plus two, floor G is plus six, and floor H is plus eleven

names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: the number of ticks written as the floor number
maths_rules: B is 3 ticks above A, so −9; C is 6 ticks above A, so −6.
F is 1 above E, so +2; G = +6 and H = +11 by counting the ticks above E.
Check: C is 5 ticks below D, so −1 − 5 = −6.
video_script.design: One idea: count ticks from a known floor. One floor line throughout. Method as in the solved examples.
open_questions: The figure on the right was not visible: floors B and C come from the printed solution (3 and 6 ticks above A); G = +6 and H = +11 are counted on the ticks in the printed solution; C being 5 ticks below D follows from A to D being 11 ticks.

beats.on_screen: title card Name the Floors; the floors of the tall block are drawn as a vertical line with ticks and the letters A to H; A, D and E carry numbers

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the floor line appears
marks.known: the numbers of floors A, D and E are written beside them
marks.ask: the question is written into the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the floors of Ruhee, drawn as a line.
<bookmark mark='known'/>The bottom floor is minus twelve, floor D is minus one, and floor E is plus one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the numbers of floors B, C, F, G and H.

beats.on_screen: the floor line stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the floor line with the ticks lit one by one; a count of plus one is written at each tick going up

marks.tick: the ticks on the line are lit one by one
marks.way: the solved example from the book is shown beside the line
marks.count: a plus one is written for each tick going up and a minus one for each tick going down

narration: <bookmark mark='tick'/>Each tick on the line is one floor.
<bookmark mark='way'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Going up one tick adds one to the number, and going down one tick takes one away.

beats.on_screen: Given: Floor A = −12; Floor D = −1; Floor E = +1

marks.given: the line Given is written on the working board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the bottom floor is minus twelve, floor D is minus one, and floor E is plus one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the numbers of Floors B, C, F, G and H

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the numbers of floors B, C, F, G and H.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: B is 3 ticks above A = −12: −11, −10, −9, so B = −9

marks.b: floor B is circled three ticks above floor A
marks.count: the three ticks are lit one by one with their numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step one, floor B lies three ticks above the bottom floor.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Count up from minus twelve, minus eleven, minus ten, and then minus nine.
Floor B is minus nine.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: C is 6 ticks above A, 3 more than B: −8, −7, −6, so C = −6

marks.c: floor C is circled six ticks above floor A
marks.count2: the next three ticks are lit one by one with their numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step two, floor C lies six ticks above the bottom floor.
<bookmark mark='count2'/>That is three more ticks than floor B. Count on from minus nine, minus eight, minus seven, and then minus six.
Floor C is minus six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: F is 1 tick above E = +1, so F = +2

marks.f: floor F is circled one tick above floor E and plus two is written

narration: <bookmark mark='f'/>Step three, floor F lies one tick above floor E.
One more than plus one is plus two, so floor F is plus two.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: count the ticks up from E: G = +6 and H = +11

marks.gh: the ticks are lit one by one above floor E
marks.six: plus six is written beside floor G and plus eleven beside floor H

narration: <bookmark mark='gh'/>Step four, count the ticks up from floor E.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Floor G is plus six, and floor H is plus eleven.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check C by counting down from D = −1, 5 ticks: −2, −3, −4, −5, −6

marks.check: the count starts at floor D
marks.back: five ticks are lit one by one going down and minus six is ticked beside floor C

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check floor C by counting down from floor D, which is minus one.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Five ticks down gives minus two, minus three, minus four, minus five, and minus six.
Both counts agree.

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed on the working board
marks.pay: the counts from the known floors are shown together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Floor B is minus nine, and floor C is minus six.
Floor F is plus two, floor G is plus six, and floor H is plus eleven.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Count the ticks from a floor you know to find the number of any floor.
